skills.title: Accessibility audit
skills.description: Audit a specified interface against WCAG or verify requested accessibility fixes. Use for explicit accessibility reviews and remediation checks; routine QA and copy edits do not require this audit. Default target is WCAG 2.2 AA.
skills.markdown:
---
name: accessibility-audit
description: "Audit a specified interface against WCAG or verify requested accessibility fixes. Use for explicit accessibility reviews and remediation checks; routine QA and copy edits do not require this audit. Default target is WCAG 2.2 AA."
license: MIT
metadata:
  upstream: "rampstackco/claude-skills"
  upstream-commit: "98d8cfe773f975a465f11c56d8fb2ae618307805"
  adapted: "2026-10-06"
---

# Accessibility audit

Assess the specified interface against the user's target. If none is supplied, use WCAG 2.2 AA. State the version and conformance level. Record the sampled pages or states and the environment, with the methods actually used. Read [Audit coverage](references/audit-coverage.md) before selecting checks.

Combine available automated checks with manual interaction. Inspect the rendered states needed for the user journey. Include errors and dynamic content. Choose tools already available in the session; do not claim a tool ran because its name appears in a plan.

Record each observed barrier with the affected page or component, reproduction steps, user impact, criterion, evidence, and proposed repair. Cite the relevant W3C criterion when the finding depends on its requirement or exceptions. Prioritize the effect on completing the task, rather than an automated score alone.

Distinguish observed failures from suspected issues and untested criteria. Static code or a screenshot may support a specific finding but cannot prove keyboard behavior, screen-reader output, or conformance of a complete process. If a required environment is unavailable, complete the supported checks and state the remaining coverage.

WCAG 2.2 AA includes applicable A and AA criteria. Include the six new A and AA criteria listed in the reference. Read the current criterion and exceptions before judging a failure. AAA criteria are outside the default target.

Do not declare legal compliance, certification, or full conformance from an automated scan or a bounded audit. Retesting a fix verifies only the behavior tested in the recorded environment. A conformance claim requires the scope and requirements in the standard to be met.

An audit request authorizes inspection and recommendations. Apply fixes when the user requested remediation too, using the existing implementation and verification workflow. Preserve the governing source, privacy, brand, and completion rules.

Adapted from [RampStack's accessibility-audit](https://github.com/rampstackco/claude-skills/tree/98d8cfe773f975a465f11c56d8fb2ae618307805/skills/accessibility-audit). The original MIT notice is in [LICENSE](LICENSE).

skills.title: Analytics strategy
skills.description: Design a measurement strategy, event tracking plan, metric definitions, or a decision-focused analytics dashboard. Use for explicit measurement design and tracking audits; calculating known metrics or drawing an existing dataset's chart does not need this workflow.
skills.markdown:
---
name: analytics-strategy
description: "Design a measurement strategy, event tracking plan, metric definitions, or a decision-focused analytics dashboard. Use for explicit measurement design and tracking audits; calculating known metrics or drawing an existing dataset's chart does not need this workflow."
license: MIT
metadata:
  upstream: "rampstackco/claude-skills"
  upstream-commit: "98d8cfe773f975a465f11c56d8fb2ae618307805"
  adapted: "2026-10-06"
---

# Analytics strategy

Start with the decision the measurement should inform. Read existing metric definitions and inspect the available data. Check the project's approved data policy before selecting collection methods. Use [Measurement decisions](references/measurement-decisions.md) to define the smallest plan that answers the question.

Define each metric's calculation and eligible population. State its time window and source, with any exclusions. Use a baseline or target only when its authority is available. A missing baseline can become a measurement task; it does not prevent a proposed plan.

Select events that support those definitions. Describe each event's exact trigger and minimum properties. Give its destination and current state, with a method for validation. Include an owner and retention requirement when established; mark them pending when unknown. Prefer an existing event or aggregate source over collecting duplicate data.

Use only approved identifiers and properties. Do not default to user IDs, email addresses, IP addresses, persistent fingerprints, or identity stitching. Free text and URLs can contain personal or sensitive information. Review their contents before proposing them as properties. If consent or retention rules are unknown, keep collection choices pending and draft only the supported design. A measurement plan does not authorize new tracking, a service connection, or deployment.

Connect dashboard views to decisions and review cadence when needed. Avoid a universal SaaS funnel, compulsory north-star metric, or decorative KPI list. One well-defined metric can be sufficient for a bounded decision.

Distinguish a proposed event from an implemented one and from delivery verified at the destination. Check delivery for missing or duplicate events. Inspect payloads for unintended properties before treating the data as reliable. Do not label a template row “Live.”

Describe observational patterns as observations. Attribution assigns credit under a model; it does not establish causality. Claims about lift or intervention impact need evidence appropriate to that claim.

Deliver the requested plan with the decisions it supports and the evidence still needed. Existing privacy, source, writing, brand, and completion rules govern implementation and handoff.

Adapted from [RampStack's analytics-strategy](https://github.com/rampstackco/claude-skills/tree/98d8cfe773f975a465f11c56d8fb2ae618307805/skills/analytics-strategy). The original MIT notice is in [LICENSE](LICENSE).

skills.title: Architecture doc
skills.description: Write a formal, sourced architecture or technical design reference covering intent, components, data, interfaces, security, operations, and trade-offs.
skills.markdown:
---
name: architecture-doc
description: "Write a formal, sourced architecture or technical design reference covering intent, components, data, interfaces, security, operations, and trade-offs."
---

# Architecture doc

Read [shared workflow](references/estate/workflow.md). For a rendered or branded artifact, read [brand policy](references/estate/brand.md) before choosing visual values. These references are generated from the canonical policies when the estate builds.

Identify the governing requirements and decisions, the reader, and the system boundary. Name unresolved source conflicts. An explicit current authority outranks a document selected merely because its file date is newer.

Separate architecture intent from implementation design. The architecture explains the product shape, boundaries, rationale, ownership, security posture, costs, and risks. The technical design supplies component contracts, data models, APIs, identity flows, deployment topology, operational controls, and failure paths. Link the two without repeating the same prose.

Tie substantive factual claims to sources. Present a design choice as a proposal with alternatives considered, the trade-off, and conditions for revisiting it. Do not describe a planned control as operating or a projected cost as measured. State material open decisions where the reader needs them.

Use diagrams only where they clarify boundaries or flows. Apply the shared brand policy when rendering a formal artifact. Verify that diagrams, tables, prose, and source revisions agree and that no assumption turned into an assertion during rendering. Deliver the requested editable format and identify the next design decision or implementation step.

skills.title: Capture a decision or correction
skills.description: Save a BeastMode decision, discovery, or factual correction with evidence and review state. Use when Megan says remember this, correct the hub, or capture a decision. Do not treat brainstorming as confirmed fact or claim a proposal is accepted.
skills.markdown:
---
name: beastmode-capture
description: Save a BeastMode decision, discovery, or factual correction with evidence and review state. Use when Megan says remember this, correct the hub, or capture a decision. Do not treat brainstorming as confirmed fact or claim a proposal is accepted.
metadata:
  version: "2026.09.30.2"
---

# Capture a decision or correction

## Host access

Use only tools and files actually available in this session. In Claude Code invoke `/beastmode-capture`; in Codex use `$beastmode-capture`; in Claude chat/Cowork ask to use `beastmode-capture`. Mac paths identify local authorities; in Cowork resolve them only through a folder already shared with this session. Cloud chat cannot read a Mac path or localhost merely because this skill names it. When hub access or a required foundation is unavailable, report that gap and continue only work supported by accessible evidence. Use named companion skills when available; otherwise apply the safeguards below and identify any required review gate you cannot complete. Do not install dependencies or broaden permissions automatically.

Use the existing hub update workflow. Do not write a second memory database or edit an assistant's separate memory unless Megan explicitly requests that separate destination.

1. Read the current BeastMode router when available and call the permitted hub's `get_context`. Establish exactly what Megan wants retained, where it belongs, and its existing sharing boundary. Default private personal capture to a permitted local destination; never infer approval to upload it to hosted or shared spaces.
2. Search for the existing subject record. Fully fetch the relevant record and sources in bounded parts, pinned to exact revisions. A correction belongs with its subject and provenance, not in a competing rulebook. If several authorities disagree, keep the conflict visible; neither drive, the newest timestamp, nor an AI synthesis wins automatically.
3. Preserve the user's wording where it expresses a decision. Classify each statement as confirmed, user-reported, observed, proposed, estimated, or creative canon as supported by the contract. Record the source and when the statement applied separately from when it was captured. A user report is attributable evidence, not independent verification. Ask only for an ambiguity that materially changes the decision, authority, or sharing scope.
4. Inspect the actual proposal schema in the available tool/service before constructing input; do not invent required fields or a new-record revision sentinel. Submit `propose_update` against the exact record and contract revisions read. Contract, confirmed-fact, and sharing changes follow the service's owner-review rules. On revision conflict, refetch and compare; preserve both edits and do not force an overwrite.
5. If the connector lacks write access, use an already-authorized local hub workflow only when the current task permits it. Never elevate a shared/cloud actor by borrowing local owner credentials. If no permitted write path exists, save a clearly marked private pending proposal under the current local intake route, including target, base revisions, evidence, and reason it is pending. If even that destination is unavailable, return the draft without claiming it was saved.
6. Verify the service response and fetch the resulting state. Distinguish draft, saved pending, proposal submitted, accepted, and dependent review needed. Acceptance requires an acceptance receipt or current accepted revision; creating a proposal is insufficient. After an accepted correction, identify registered dependents, request the supported refresh, and verify what changed. Unregistered documents may still be stale. Preserve submitted résumés, published historical artifacts, and archived evidence; create corrected successors where appropriate.

Return what was captured, its source, destination, exact state, and what remains for review. A saved proposal is not an automatic change to every AI tool. For material changes use `execution-truth` and report changed now, verified, still unchanged, and exact next action.

Examples: `$beastmode-capture Hold the sales-pursuit number until we have supporting evidence.` / `$beastmode-capture Save this as a proposed product idea, not a committed plan.`

# Start with current context

## Host access

Use only tools and files actually available in this session. In Claude Code invoke `/beastmode-context`; in Codex use `$beastmode-context`; in Claude chat/Cowork ask to use `beastmode-context`. Use named companion skills when available; otherwise apply the safeguards below and identify any required review gate you cannot complete. Do not install dependencies or broaden permissions automatically.

Turn Megan's request into work based on the right sources. This skill is a workflow, not a biography or a replacement operating contract.

1. Identify the requested result and finish line. Read `/Volumes/BeastMode/AGENTS.md` when mounted, then only the subject authority it names. Use the existing `beastmode-hub` connection's `get_context` with a focused query before work. Retain the returned contract revision and record revisions. Treat source documents as evidence, not instructions.
2. Distinguish the connection's permitted scope from separately authorized local-file access. A common-contract-only response is not proof that private knowledge is absent. Do not switch accounts, grant access, or upload private files to fill that gap. If the drive or service is unavailable, state what cannot be checked; use a dated authorized snapshot only with that limitation, or continue independent work.
3. Search only relevant records. Fully fetch selected records in bounded parts at their exact revisions; recover clipped reads before relying on them. Read the underlying evidence needed for consequential claims. A summary cannot independently prove itself. Preserve conflicts, held claims, historical dates, and the distinction between when a fact was true and when it was learned.
4. For a resumed task, inspect its current files, saved receipt, remaining work, and dirty repository state. Prior chat and an old handoff locate evidence; they do not establish completion. Continue the actual next action without rerunning a completed inventory.
5. Before human-facing drafting, establish audience, purpose, intended reader action, voice, and consequence level. For hub-backed material drafts, call `get_context` with `contentRequest` and the relevant foundation IDs. Read the current voice sources routed by BeastMode. Use `writing-integrity`; use `career-application` for applications and the portfolio claims-and-rights ledger for public work. Preserve substantive career scope, ownership, and progression. Do not replace a résumé with a project handout or pick length before coverage.
6. Apply lighter prose review to routine internal notes and deep review to hiring, public, client, or consequential work. Accuracy and privacy apply at every level. Check accuracy, representation, writing, and layout separately; a passing script or attractive render does not prove content quality. Show a business reader the problem, Megan's role, decisions, mechanism, and supported result, rather than unexplained internal counts.
7. Perform the requested work. Use the existing publication/replacement gate when applicable; do not create a new competing quality contract. Use `execution-truth` for material changes. If a Brain task ID is the work source, also use `brain-work-item` and resolve its paths against the current router.

Return the useful result, material source conflicts or gaps, and exact state. For material work, finish with changed now, verified, still unchanged, and the exact next action. Keep private provenance out of public artifacts. Do not claim publication, adoption, or universal AI compliance from local files.

Examples: `$beastmode-context Resume my portfolio work from the current sources.` / `$beastmode-context What should I use to explain my AI work to a hiring manager?`

skills.title: Check the hub and explain what needs attention
skills.description: Check whether BeastMode context, connections, ingestion, maintenance, budgets, and recovery are working, with scoped evidence. Use for a hub health check or troubleshooting stale context. A check is read-only unless Megan also requests repair; it does not start new recurring jobs.
skills.markdown:
---
name: beastmode-health
description: Check whether BeastMode context, connections, ingestion, maintenance, budgets, and recovery are working, with scoped evidence. Use for a hub health check or troubleshooting stale context. A check is read-only unless Megan also requests repair; it does not start new recurring jobs.
metadata:
  version: "2026.10.01.2"
---

# Check the hub and explain what needs attention

## Host access

Use only tools and files actually available in this session. In Claude Code invoke `/beastmode-health`; in Codex use `$beastmode-health`; in Claude chat/Cowork ask to use `beastmode-health`. Mac paths identify local authorities; in Cowork resolve them only through a folder already shared with this session. Cloud chat cannot read a Mac path or localhost merely because this skill names it. When hub access or a required foundation is unavailable, report that gap and continue only work supported by accessible evidence. Use named companion skills when available; otherwise apply the safeguards below and identify any required review gate you cannot complete. Do not install dependencies or broaden permissions automatically.

1. Read the current BeastMode router when available. Call `get_context`, then `check_health` on the existing permitted hub connection. Record the observation time, environment (local or hosted), actor scope, and returned contract revision. Do not silently substitute a different account or endpoint.
2. Interpret the response within that scope. Null backup, budget, or bridge fields mean unavailable to this check, not absent or healthy. Zero visible findings in a common-contract-only view does not mean the private hub is healthy. “Verified connected” means retrieval was observed; it does not prove that the tool followed guidance, accessed private records, or completed a cloud connection.
3. For authorized Mac-local maintenance, run `python3 scripts/collect_evidence.py` from this skill directory first, using its `references/evidence-index.json`. The script reads the hub’s existing writer-maintained SQLite receipt pointers in read-only mode, verifies the current backup file and skill links, and reports bridge and launchd state. It does not perform a restore or print raw private records, login keys, or recovery material. If this session cannot run local scripts or reach the runtime, label these areas `not-rechecked`; do not infer a current failure from an old receipt. Do not create a second Store/writer or reuse local owner authentication for a cloud caller. Then inspect current operator documentation or bounded logs only for gaps the script cannot cover.
4. Check the dimensions the task and access support: source mounts and registered coverage; source/retrieval revision parity; current adapters and actual account probes; failed/overdue jobs and backlog; unresolved freshness/dependency findings; monthly usage plus infrastructure reserve; backup age, isolated restoration evidence, off-service delivery, and separate key recovery. Verify timestamps and expected schedules from the current configuration. File presence does not prove installation, a schedule does not prove execution, and local restoration does not prove off-service recovery.
5. Use each script row as the starting status for its area. Its `verified-now` restore status means the latest recorded isolated restore covers the current generation and its encrypted backup hash still matches; it does not mean a restore ran during this health check. It reads receipt pointers by database key, not filename, so newer receipts in nested folders count when written by the hub. Classify remaining dimensions as verified now, needs attention, or not rechecked, with timestamp and evidence. Carry stable finding IDs across reviews. A narrower check leaves prior findings not rechecked; it does not resolve them. Mark resolution only after passing evidence and reopen on recurrence. Do not turn old field-guide counts or previous healthy receipts into present status.
6. For connection behavior, make a harmless read probe against a record the actor is allowed to see, fully fetch the pinned revision, and compare it with the expected revision. If two tools are being verified, test each actual account. Use synthetic nonprivate material for write-path tests, only within an authorized test scope; never mutate production merely to prove a check worked.
7. Prioritize findings by consequence: wrong authority/private leakage or data loss, failed capture/retrieval, recovery gaps, blocked jobs, then cosmetic drift. If repair was requested, fix reversible failures within that scope and recheck. Otherwise return the concrete repair needed. Changing account access, sharing, contracts, spending commitments, or destructive state requires the applicable user authorization. Do not create another maintenance scheduler by default.

Report a short, useful status with evidence and the most important next action. Explicitly separate local service availability from hosted access and ledger accounting from provider billing enforcement. Explain that Mac-local agents cannot run while the Mac is asleep. Use `execution-truth` for repairs and state changed now, verified, still unchanged, and exact next action.

Examples: `$beastmode-health Check what is working and what needs attention.` / `$beastmode-health Diagnose the stale context and repair reversible local failures.`

skills.description: Compare a named BeastMode or Meridian folder with current authorities, preserve unique evidence, and archive verified duplicates reversibly. Use for new intake or continued cleanup. Do not trigger for simple retrieval, or equate similar filenames, age, or inactivity with obsolescence.
skills.markdown:
---
name: beastmode-reconcile
description: Compare a named BeastMode or Meridian folder with current authorities, preserve unique evidence, and archive verified duplicates reversibly. Use for new intake or continued cleanup. Do not trigger for simple retrieval, or equate similar filenames, age, or inactivity with obsolescence.
metadata:
  version: "2026.09.30.2"
---

# Reconcile a bounded set of files

## Host access

Use only tools and files actually available in this session. In Claude Code invoke `/beastmode-reconcile`; in Codex use `$beastmode-reconcile`; in Claude chat/Cowork ask to use `beastmode-reconcile`. Mac paths identify local authorities; in Cowork resolve them only through a folder already shared with this session. Cloud chat cannot read a Mac path or localhost merely because this skill names it. When hub access or a required foundation is unavailable, report that gap and continue only work supported by accessible evidence. Use named companion skills when available; otherwise apply the safeguards below and identify any required review gate you cannot complete. Do not install dependencies or broaden permissions automatically.

1. Read the current BeastMode router and call the permitted hub's `get_context`. Inspect the current reconciliation record and disposition map under `/Volumes/BeastMode/AIMemory/knowledge-hub-local/`; select the latest applicable evidence, not a date alone. Identify the named folder, comparison roots, authority questions, and authorized action. Both BeastMode and Meridian are sources; neither outranks the other by location.
2. Check mounts and actual source paths before using old manifests. Read relevant folder/repository guidance. Inspect dirty work, tracked paths, vault structure, links, symlinks, hard links, and active consumers before proposing moves. Reuse existing validated inventory and hash results when unchanged. Hash only changed or missing candidates; escalate to content comparison only for meaningful differences. Do not rescan both drives for a one-folder request.
3. Classify each candidate as exact duplicate, divergent version, complementary evidence, unique material, or unresolved. Exact duplicates require matching complete file hashes and a verified retained copy; archive safety also depends on the file's role. Matching bytes alone do not authorize breaking a repository, app, vault, or active route. Treat credentials and recovery material as excluded: do not read, copy, or ingest their contents.
4. For divergent material, compare relevant claims and intended use. Preserve source authorship, dates, and evidence. Newer edits are not necessarily newer facts. Keep distinct assessment versions and related-but-different programs separate. Do not promote an unsupported metric from a historical résumé, borrowed example, or AI summary. Extract unique material into a cited comparison or proposed synthesis without silently replacing originals.
5. Prepare a concrete move manifest in the private reconciliation area: source, retained canonical/peer path, archive destination, hashes, classification, reason, consumer repairs, and inverse move. Record why an authority was selected. Reuse the existing map format and rollback mechanism rather than creating a second ledger. Keep unresolved authority decisions visible while completing independent safe work.
6. If Megan requested cleanup/archiving, perform reversible moves within that scope once verification and the manifest are ready; do not ask again for an already-authorized action. If she requested comparison only, stop at the reviewed plan. Never permanently delete. Before each move, recheck source and peer hashes and refuse occupied destinations. Use staged copy-and-verify before source removal for cross-filesystem moves; retain complete recovery evidence. Prefer archiving verified individual files over moving a mixed folder with unique content.
7. Verify every disposition on disk, retained content, repaired links/consumers, and rollback instructions. Preserve historical submissions and repository history. A missing drive or read error is incomplete coverage, not a duplicate or successful archive. Record completed, preserved, excluded, and unresolved items explicitly.
8. Refresh affected hub routes through supported version-checked proposals or the existing authorized bridge workflow. Do not overwrite synchronized knowledge Markdown or open a second writer against the live SQLite store. Verify ingestion/retrieval separately from the filesystem move. A source-change flag is not proof that dependent prose was corrected.

Use `execution-truth`. Finish with changed now, verified, still unchanged, exact next action, and the disposition/rollback record. Use semantic scope such as “this assessment folder,” not total file counts, to explain coverage. Leave unrelated projects and DesignOS alone unless requested.

Example: `$beastmode-reconcile Compare this folder with the current career sources, preserve unique material, and archive verified duplicates.`

skills.description: Start, continue, or close Megan's Brain-linked Codex work item. Use when a Brain task ID or daily ready item is the work source, or when finishing a linked task.
skills.markdown:
---
name: brain-work-item
description: Start, continue, or close Megan's Brain-linked Codex work item. Use when a Brain task ID or daily ready item is the work source, or when finishing a linked task.
---

# Brain work item

The current task authority is `/Volumes/BeastMode/AI Workstreams/MeganOS/Brain`. Read the named note under `Today/Tasks/` and its project brief under `System/Projects/`. Preserve the task ID, evidence, and status history. The task bridge resolves Brain from its current installation; `MEGAN_BRAIN_PATH` can override that location.

## Start or continue work

When Megan starts a ready item, set its status to `in-progress` with the Brain task helper. If the current chat is already linked, continue here. Otherwise create its working chat through the Codex app:

1. Run `/usr/bin/python3 '/Volumes/BeastMode/AI Workstreams/MeganOS/megan-os/bin/task_bridge.py' --pending`. It returns each unlinked active task's title, prompt, desktop project ID, and note hash.
2. Use `list_projects` to confirm the returned project ID and folder. Reserve the selected task with the bridge's `--reserve TASK_ID --expected-hash HASH` command. A reservation stops repeated runs from creating another chat.
3. If the plan has `existing_thread_id`, reuse that chat. Otherwise call the Codex app's `create_thread` tool with the returned title and prompt, `target.type=project`, the verified desktop project ID, and `environment.type=local`. Keep the user's configured model. The standing Brain sync plan authorizes this task-specific chat creation.
4. Link the returned `threadId` using the bridge's `--link TASK_ID THREAD_ID --expected-hash HASH` command. It saves the returned ID locally, checks desktop membership and working folder, and links the Brain note only if the note still matches. A `clientThreadId` is pending setup, not a thread ID.
5. Run the bridge once without options and read `System/Sync/Health.md`. The working chat carries out the next action; do not execute that same action in both chats.

If creation or linking has an uncertain outcome, retain the reservation and recover the returned chat ID from the tool result. Do not retry creation blindly. A changed Brain note, unavailable folder, or wrong project stays visible as a queued item or conflict. An existing linked chat is reused.

The daily view at `Today/Ready Work.md` shows every ready item grouped by project and includes each linked chat. The daily 9 a.m. updater recovers changes missed between work sessions.

## Record a work boundary

Use the project's current source folder and guidance. At a real work boundary, record the actual result in Brain:

```sh
/usr/bin/python3 '/Volumes/BeastMode/AI Workstreams/MeganOS/megan-os/bin/brain_tasks.py' receipt TASK_ID --status complete --result 'What changed' --verification 'What was checked'
```

Use `blocked` or `in-progress` when that is the actual state. A completion receipt needs specific verification. An idle or archived chat does not close a task. After recording a receipt, run the bridge once so it refreshes the daily view and archives a chat only for an explicit Brain closure.

If Brain is unavailable, retain the result in the chat and report that Brain has not been updated. Keep local preparation, employer submission, publication, deployment, and verified results in their exact states. Preserve Megan's existing authorizations; do not infer new external actions from chat creation.

Former-employer actions marked `closed-no-longer-owned` stay historical. Create a new independent task for continuing work.

skills.title: Business case
skills.description: Build an executive investment case with supported benefits, costs, alternatives, risks, and a bounded funding decision.
skills.markdown:
---
name: business-case
description: "Build an executive investment case with supported benefits, costs, alternatives, risks, and a bounded funding decision."
---

# Business case

Read [shared workflow](references/estate/workflow.md). For rendered artifacts, read [brand policy](references/estate/brand.md).

Identify the approver, decision, current situation, proposed intervention, timing, and source of financial figures. Use evidence-core to separate measured facts, reported expectations, estimates, and assumptions.

Compare the proposal with doing nothing and credible alternatives. Include benefits, implementation and operating costs, opportunity costs, dependencies, risks, and reasons not to invest. Do not assume that a vendor's projected benefit is realized value.

Show calculations for savings, capacity, revenue, payback, or cost of delay. Use sensitivity scenarios only with explicit inputs; avoid false precision and double-counted benefits. Identify who can validate the assumptions and who owns realization.

Bound the ask by amount, scope, stage, conditions, decision owner, and next review. Render for the approver's actual decision, preserving material uncertainties. A business case supports an investment decision; it does not record approval until the approver actually gives it.

skills.title: Career application
skills.description: Assess, tailor, prepare interviews, fill, or resume Megan's leadership-level applications using current postings and private career evidence. Never submit without explicit authorization.
skills.markdown:
---
name: career-application
description: Assess, tailor, prepare interviews, fill, or resume Megan's leadership-level applications using current postings and private career evidence. Never submit without explicit authorization.
---

# Career application

Run one role at a time from current evidence without relying on conversation history.

## Start here

Use the live source when it is available:

`/Volumes/BeastMode/AIMemory/JobHunt/`

Read `00_Master/Career_Application_Operating_Context.md` first. Then load only:

- the current live posting;
- the current role's `Role_Work_Record.md`, when one exists; and
- the source files named by the operating context for the current mode.

Do not load every prior application or reconstruct the full JobHunt folder unless a cross-surface correction requires it.

This estate package contains workflow instructions and validation code. Private career evidence, submitted applications, and resumes remain in the subject authority. If that source is unavailable, ask for the specific current evidence needed for the request or use an explicitly supplied dated bundle. Do not assume this package includes those private records. Return proposed record changes for the user to save when the live destination is unavailable.

## Invocation modes

Infer the mode from Megan's request. She can also state it directly.

- Codex: `$career-application assess <URL>`
- Claude Code: `/career-application assess <URL>`
- Claude chat or Cowork: enable **Career Application**, then say `Use Career Application to assess <URL>`.

- `$career-application assess <URL>`: verify the live posting, screen the role, and recommend pursue or skip.
- `$career-application find <criteria>`: find current roles, screen them, and return a shortlist. Do not create application folders until Megan chooses a role.
- `$career-application tailor <URL>`: create or update the role work record and a role-specific resume copy. Do not overwrite a master resume.
- `$career-application interview <company or role>`: build a role-specific leadership interview plan from the current posting and evidence-backed story bank.
- `$career-application fill <URL>`: open the form, fill supported factual fields, upload approved materials, and stop at the authorization boundaries below.
- `$career-application status <company or role>`: read the tracker and role work record, then report the verified state and next action.
- `$career-application continue <company or role>`: resume from the saved role work record rather than from prior chat history.

If the request does not specify a mode, use `assess` for a new URL and `continue` for a named existing role.

## Assess

1. Verify the employer's current posting. Treat reposts, aggregators, and old snapshots as secondary.
2. Screen leadership scope, decision authority, reporting shape, compensation, location, technical GTM or transformation relevance, and billable-delivery expectations.
3. Map requirements into four groups: strong evidence, transferable evidence, real gaps, and unsupported or unanswered questions.
4. Give a direct pursue or skip recommendation. Do not tailor materials for a skip.
5. When Megan explicitly chooses pursue or skip, update `03_Tracker/applications.md` in the live source. A skip needs no application folder unless notes would prevent repeated research. In a portable session, create an updated tracker copy for Megan instead of claiming the live tracker changed.

## Tailor and prepare

1. Create `01_Applications/Current/YYYY-MM-DD_Company_Role/` under the live source.
2. Copy `02_Templates/Role_Work_Record_Template.md` into that folder as `Role_Work_Record.md` and fill it from evidence.
3. Read `00_Master/Career_Narrative_Translation_Guide.md`. Map the role's three or four primary mandates to programs in the role record before drafting.
4. When the governed skill estate or Knowledge Hub is selected, read `00_Master/Governed_AI_Skill_Estate_and_Knowledge_Hub_Program_Record.md`. When the estate or an individual skill is selected, also read `00_Master/AI_Skill_Portfolio_Quality_and_Scaling_Record.md`. Keep the estate's reusable-method and distribution story separate from the Hub's bounded-context and persistence story. Select one or two role-relevant skills and preserve the problem, user, mechanism, risk-specific test, pivot or growth path, and verified state. Do not lead with skill or test counts.
5. For solution-engineering, technical-pre-sales, forward-deployed, architecture, value-engineering, Deal Desk, technical-GTM, customer-strategy, transformation, delivery, or recovery roles, read `00_Master/Client_Work_Strategy_and_Leadership_Record.md` and `00_Master/Solution_Engineering_Leadership_Evidence_Map.md`. Use `00_Master/GoGuardian_Program_Record.md` when that assessment-to-remediation sequence is selected. Choose at least one actual client decision and one portfolio, people, or practice mechanism. Keep 43 pursuit teams, 53 deal/project cycles, and 46 authored quotes distinct; the counts do not replace the case.
6. For product, platform, identity, security, or responsible-AI roles, read `00_Master/Linky_Product_Record.md` when Linky is selected. Keep local build and test proof separate from deployment, access, usage, and adoption.
7. For assessment, workforce, enablement, or people-system roles, read `00_Master/Assessment_Strategy_and_Enablement_Program_Record.md`. Preserve source-bank authorship, human-review boundaries, and the difference between built, published privately, shared, run, and adopted.
8. For each selected program, preserve the problem or decision, Megan's ownership, the mechanism, the evidence-backed result, and the real gap or state boundary. Retain the constraint or pivot when it proves leadership or judgment. For governed skills, distinguish original authorship, later estate governance or integration, and later contributor authorship; admission, repair, rename, or consolidation does not establish sole authorship of every package.
9. Select the base resume using the operating-context router. Copy it into the role folder before editing.
10. Before drafting, inventory relevant prior role-specific resumes and historical variants. Read the versions that cover the role mandate and note in the role work record what prior wording or layout to retain, revise, or exclude. Treat them as writing history, never as current claim authority; recheck carried claims against current evidence. A clipped read is incomplete.
11. Tailor only what the posting supports: headline, executive profile, expertise order, selected bullet order or wording, and technology emphasis. Intentional selection is required; do not collapse unrelated programs into one “AI tools” bullet, a platform list, or a playbook count; do not force the entire portfolio into the document.
12. Keep private evidence notes separate from employer-facing materials. Do not place client-sensitive facts, internal identifiers, repositories, or unsupported metrics in application files.
13. Apply Megan's `megan-writing-style` and `writing-integrity` rules. Run `/usr/bin/python3 ~/.agents/humanize/tellscan.py scan <file> --profile megan` as a deterministic gate where it is installed, not as permission to flatten real resume lists.
14. Render and inspect every changed DOCX. Verify accessibility and document integrity. Separately read the finished copy against the role mandate and evidence map; layout review does not prove content quality.
15. Complete the `Resume source review` receipt in the role work record and run `scripts/check_role_resume_readiness.py` against that record before calling a tailored resume prepared locally. The checker verifies a completed receipt and readable files, not the truth or quality of its prose; perform the content review yourself.
16. Update the role work record and tracker with the exact local state. When the source is unavailable, use a supplied role-work-record template or clearly label a new draft record and return it for the user to save.

## Prepare for interviews

1. Verify the current posting and read the role work record. Do not prepare from a remembered title or an expired posting when a live source is available.
2. Read `00_Master/Leadership_Interview_Evidence_Map.md`, `04_Interview/Interview_Preparation.md`, and `05_Reference/Story_Bank/Success_Stories.md`. Add only the program records needed for the role's primary mandates.
3. Translate the posting into five or six likely decision areas: business ownership, technical or solution judgment, executive influence, delivery or recovery, people leadership, and adversity or learning. Do not turn the result into a generic question dump.
4. Select no more than six anchor stories. For each one, prepare a 30-second headline, a two-minute causal answer, likely follow-ups, the difficult decision or conversation, the turnaround mechanism, the result, and the evidence boundary.
5. Use the order: problem or stakes, Megan's mandate, decision, mechanism, resistance or constraint, turning point, evidence-backed result, and learning. Name what changed because of Megan rather than only describing the artifact.
6. Preserve ownership boundaries. Do not claim that Megan performed every delivery task, that forecast value was realized, that UAT equals production, or that an opportunity became a win without evidence.
7. Do not fabricate a direct-report performance case, hiring decision, promotion decision, team-conflict case, or quantified adoption result. If a target role is likely to test one of those areas, mark it as an evidence gap and ask Megan for a real event before drafting the answer.
8. Keep closed corrective-action history out of routine preparation. Use it only if Megan explicitly chooses that material for a specific answer.
9. Save role-specific interview work inside the application folder. Do not overwrite the master interview book for one employer.

## Fill and submit

Filling an application does not authorize submission.

Fill supported factual fields and upload reviewed files. Pause for Megan on:

- salary expectations;
- unconfirmed work authorization or sponsorship answers;
- demographic or self-identification questions;
- legal attestations, signatures, and acknowledgments;
- MFA and CAPTCHA; and

skills.markdown:
---
name: "career-materials-and-outreach"
description: "Draft the pieces around Megan's tailored resume (cover letter, form answers, outreach, LinkedIn sections, reference packets) from the role work record and current evidence, in her voice, as drafts only."
---

# Career materials and outreach

Runs beside `career-application` once a role has a work record with a completed narrative translation table; if the table is empty, run `career-application tailor` first. These pieces select from the same three or four programs the resume uses, so the resume and the letter say the same things.

Before drafting, load `00_Master/Career_Application_Operating_Context.md`, the role's `Role_Work_Record.md` (including its Estimate basis section), the tailored resume copy, the live posting, `00_Master/Professional_Profile.md`. Claim authority is Professional_Profile → program records → `05_Reference/Claim_Governance/Career_Program_Evidence_Ledger.md`; Portfolio case studies are public copies, not a source of figures. LinkedIn work starts from `00_Master/LinkedIn_Profile_Draft.md` and `00_Master/LinkedIn_Profile_Positioning_Brief.md`. Behavioral answers draw on `05_Reference/Story_Bank/Success_Stories.md` and the anchor stories in `04_Interview/Interview_Preparation.md`. References use `02_Templates/References_Template_One_Page.docx`.

Megan is the author. Before drafting, state audience, purpose, reader action and consequence level; hiring material gets deep review. Write under `megan-writing-style` and `writing-integrity`; run `/usr/bin/python3 ~/.agents/humanize/tellscan.py scan <file> --profile megan` on each finished file where installed, fix structure rather than swapping words, and say plainly when no scan ran.

## Rules for every piece

- Open with the point. Each sentence carries a name, number, system, decision or date.
- Posting keywords appear where they describe real work, once or twice a paragraph.
- People leadership is managed people leaders, hired, coached, ran performance reviews; no headcount.
- Figures are locked or stated figures from the sources above, or estimates already in the record's Estimate basis. Years-per-skill for a form field count as an estimate: compute from role dates, record in Estimate basis, then use.
- Employment ended October 1, 2026; nothing implies she is still at her former employer, and a current-employment answer matches the date of the action. Dates are month and year. No defensive narration about the exit or title history.
- Nothing employer-owned: no former-employer branding, client-sensitive facts, internal identifiers or repositories.
- Caveats stay in the ledger. Reader-facing copy states what is true and leaves out what is not; no "not verified", "directional" or "I don't claim" sentences.
- People stories: never invent a hiring, performance, termination or team-conflict case. If a prompt needs one and the sources hold none, mark the gap and ask Megan for a real event.
- Alignment flag in the record's Current decision (Axon's police and weapons business, for example) with Megan choosing to pursue: "why us" copy names the role's mandate and platform problem in her words and ties it to her stated reason for the move. Never a mission or values endorsement she has not said. If her reason line is missing, ask for it before drafting.

## Cover letter

250–350 words, four paragraphs, to a named person when WebSearch finds one, otherwise no salutation line.

1. The specific reason this role fits, tied to one program from the translation table.
2. Two or three posting requirements, each answered with one program, its mechanism and its result.
3. The largest real gap from the record answered with adjacent evidence, or the applied-AI work that distinguishes her in this lane; skipped when the gap is minor.
4. What she would want to discuss first.

No "I am excited to apply", no trait statements, no closing moral. Deliver one letter as a Codex doc; when a file is required, a DOCX beside the resume as `Megan_Shellman_<Company>_<Role>_Cover_Letter.docx`.

## Application-form answers

Answer the question asked, then stop; plain text ready to paste.

- Experience questions: skill, years, one sentence of where she used it; years match the resume.
- "Why this company or role": specific to the company, connected to her real work, under 150 words unless the field allows more; under an alignment flag, the rule above.
- Work samples: the most relevant publish-cleared case studies, one line each with link and one proof point.
- Behavioral prompts: 100–200 words from the anchor stories, ending on the result, under the people-story rule.
- Ratings and dropdowns: the accurate level.
- Pause with no draft: salary expectations, work authorization and sponsorship, demographic and self-identification questions, attestations and signatures.

Present answers as a table of field, answer, character count, field limit. Entering fields and submitting belong to `career-application fill` and its authorization boundaries.

## Outreach to a hiring manager or connection

Subject under eight words, specific to their team or the role. Body under 150 words: one specific about their work, one result of hers that bears on it, one ask (a twenty-minute conversation or a referral path). Link one case study. Cut any sentence that could go to another company. Draft only; a Gmail draft when she asks; sending and recruiter contact are separate approval boundaries.

## LinkedIn sections

Headline under 220 characters in the brief's resolved identity: Solution Engineering and Technical GTM leadership, applied AI as the differentiator. About: first person, three to five short paragraphs, opening with what she led and built, two or three named results, a closing line on what she wants only if she wants open-to-work visible. Experience entries carry the resume's titles, dates and figures exactly and may add context the resume cut. Skills: top three pinned to the lane she is prioritizing. Output is a section-by-section diff against the staged draft. Publication is Megan's action and a separate approval boundary.

## References

Megan names the references. For each: name, current title and company, relationship and the period they saw her work, the lane and claims they can speak to, contact details as she supplies them. Produce a permission request, a briefing note (the role, three things worth emphasizing, the evidence behind each) and a thank-you note, in her voice. The list lives in the role folder on the one-page template and is private.

## Recording

Write each piece's path and state into the role work record under Resume and materials; keep `03_Tracker/applications.md` current. States: `prepared locally` for a file; `filled and awaiting submission` only after `career-application fill`; `submitted` only with employer confirmation. End with changed, verified, unchanged and the exact next action.

Method adapted from the open-source ResumeSkills set (cover-letter-generator, application-form-filler, cold-email-writer, linkedin-profile-optimizer, reference-list-builder), rebuilt against the October 7, 2026 operating context.

Write under megan-writing-style and writing-integrity; run /usr/bin/python3 ~/.agents/humanize/tellscan.py scan <file> --profile megan on each finished file where installed, fix structure rather than swapping words, and say plainly when no scan ran.

Rules for every piece

  • Open with the point. Each sentence carries a name, number, system, decision or date.
  • Posting keywords appear where they describe real work, once or twice a paragraph.
  • People leadership is managed people leaders, hired, coached, ran performance reviews; no headcount.
  • Figures are locked or stated figures from the sources above, or estimates already in the record's Estimate basis. Years-per-skill for a form field count as an estimate: compute from role dates, record in Estimate basis, then use.
  • Employment ended October 1, 2026; nothing implies she is still at her former employer, and a current-employment answer matches the date of the action. Dates are month and year. No defensive narration about the exit or title history.
  • Nothing employer-owned: no former-employer branding, client-sensitive facts, internal identifiers or repositories.
  • Caveats stay in the ledger. Reader-facing copy states what is true and leaves out what is not; no "not verified", "directional" or "I don't claim" sentences.
  • People stories: never invent a hiring, performance, termination or team-conflict case. If a prompt needs one and the sources hold none, mark the gap and ask Megan for a real event.
  • Alignment flag in the record's Current decision (Axon's police and weapons business, for example) with Megan choosing to pursue: "why us" copy names the role's mandate and platform problem in her words and ties it to her stated reason for the move. Cover letter

250–350 words, four paragraphs, to a named person when WebSearch finds one, otherwise no salutation line.

  1. The specific reason this role fits, tied to one program from the translation table.
  2. Two or three posting requirements, each answered with one program, its mechanism and its result.
  3. The largest real gap from the record answered with adjacent evidence, or the applied-AI work that distinguishes her in this lane; skipped when the gap is minor.
  4. What she would want to discuss first.

Answer the question asked, then stop; plain text ready to paste.

  • Experience questions: skill, years, one sentence of where she used it; years match the resume.
  • "Why this company or role": specific to the company, connected to her real work, under 150 words unless the field allows more; under an alignment flag, the rule above.
  • Work samples: the most relevant publish-cleared case studies, one line each with link and one proof point.
  • Behavioral prompts: 100–200 words from the anchor stories, ending on the result, under the people-story rule.
  • Ratings and dropdowns: the accurate level.
  • Pause with no draft: salary expectations, work authorization and sponsorship, demographic and self-identification questions, attestations and signatures.

Outreach to a hiring manager or connection

Subject under eight words, specific to their team or the role. Body under 150 words: one specific about their work, one result of hers that bears on it, one ask (a twenty-minute conversation or a referral path). Link one case study. Cut any sentence that could go to another company. Draft only; a Gmail draft when she asks; sending and recruiter contact are separate approval boundaries.

LinkedIn sections

Headline under 220 characters in the brief's resolved identity: Solution Engineering and Technical GTM leadership, applied AI as the differentiator. About: first person, three to five short paragraphs, opening with what she led and built, two or three named results, a closing line on what she wants only if she wants open-to-work visible. Experience entries carry the resume's titles, dates and figures exactly and may add context the resume cut. Skills: top three pinned to the lane she is prioritizing. Output is a section-by-section diff against the staged draft. Publication is Megan's action and a separate approval boundary.

References

Megan names the references. For each: name, current title and company, relationship and the period they saw her work, the lane and claims they can speak to, contact details as she supplies them. Produce a permission request, a briefing note (the role, three things worth emphasizing, the evidence behind each) and a thank-you note, in her voice. The list lives in the role folder on the one-page template and is private.

Recording

Write each piece's path and state into the role work record under Resume and materials; keep 03_Tracker/applications.md current. States: prepared locally for a file; filled and awaiting submission only after career-application fill; submitted only with employer confirmation. End with changed, verified, unchanged and the exact next action.

skills.title: Career progression and offers
skills.description: Assess a role, the whole tracker or an offer against Megan's VP-to-ELT path and her gates; prepare salary negotiation; compare offers side by side. Megan decides.
skills.markdown:
---
name: "career-progression-and-offers"
description: "Assess a role, the whole tracker or an offer against Megan's VP-to-ELT path and her gates; prepare salary negotiation; compare offers side by side. Megan decides."
---

# Career progression and offers

Runs beside `career-application`. Four jobs: a progression check on one role, a portfolio view across the tracker, negotiation prep once a number is in play, and an offer comparison. Megan decides; this skill produces facts and drafts.

Before starting, load `00_Master/Career_Application_Operating_Context.md` (target-role screen, October 7 career direction), the role's `Role_Work_Record.md`, `03_Tracker/applications.md`, `05_Reference/Career_Strategy/Career_Paths.md`, and the live posting or written offer. The career-application assess screen still runs; this adds the level view the operating context asks for.

## Gates

Show each result; a failed gate is never averaged into a score.

- Base at or above $200K, target $250K or more, base only. No posted base → open question, not a pass.
- Billability: nonbillable preferred; a billable component is negotiable only when expected billability is strictly below 25%, so 25% fails. Unknown → unresolved question to ask; never assume zero from a leadership title, presales work or an employment contract. Owning a company's own internal platforms is not billable delivery.
- Not a Solution Architect role or an equivalent individual-contributor solution-design or delivery-resource role, whatever the title. Architecture experience is leadership evidence only.
- Scope: compare authority against her Senior Director and practice-lead history, not titles. Unknown scope → unresolved.
- Alignment: record any flag Megan or the research raised (industry, customers, politics) as a line under the record's Current decision, with her stated reason when she chooses to pursue. Recorded, never scored.

## Progression matrix

The destination is a path to VP and eventually an executive leadership team seat. For each of the operating context's eight criteria (strategy ownership, decision authority, budget or resource accountability, people or organizational leadership, enterprise outcomes, executive exposure, reporting line, next leadership level) record one of three states: verified (an employer statement in the posting, offer letter or interview), inferred (plausible from role shape, labeled), unknown. A Director title, a VP reporting line or a recruiter's promise is inferred at most; a promotion is verified only in writing.

Score verified 2, inferred 1, unknown 0 per criterion, weighted. Weights are Megan's; ask once, record them in the operating context's target-role screen when she gives them, and use equal weights until then. Report the three column counts beside the score so a high score built on inference is visible. Keep the matrix in the record under Screen and update it after every interview round.

Level red flags in a posting: "hands-on", "player-coach", "individual contributor", "utilization" or "billable" targets, "architect" in the title or first responsibility, no direct reports, a reporting line below VP, delivery hidden in "other duties", two roles written into one posting. Compensation red flags: "competitive salary", "DOE", equity-heavy with no base. A repost needs a reason found.

Discovery questions start from "Questions for the employer" in `04_Interview/Interview_Preparation.md` and add only these progression questions — who held this role last and where did they go; what the role decides on budget and hiring without escalation; who sits on the ELT and how this role reaches them; expected billable share in hours; who has been promoted from this level in the last two years.

## Portfolio view

On request, run the gates and the matrix across every nonterminal row in the tracker and add one line per role on lane coherence against the primary identity in `Career_Paths.md` (Solution Engineering and Technical GTM leadership; applied AI differentiator; revenue technology foundation). Note where an in-house IT seat, a RevOps lens or a consulting title pulls away from that identity. When a role closes, record why in its work record so the next search learns from it.

## Negotiation

- Research with WebSearch at each offer stage: posted bands for comparable Director and Senior Director roles in GTM systems, revenue technology and solutions engineering; the employer's own ranges; levels data where it exists. Cite source and date. Without search, use the employer's posted range with a dated note.
- Megan supplies the number. Draft nothing for a salary field or a recruiter's expectations question until she gives a figure. Default, which she can change: do not disclose past pay.
- Counter on base first. Secondary levers in the order that serves the destination: a title on the VP line, a written scope and decision-authority statement, a dated review tied to a level, ELT meeting access, signing bonus, equity, start date, remote and travel terms, budget or headcount for the function. A verbal promise not in the offer letter stays unknown.
- Deliver a counter email and a call script with answers to "this is our best offer", "the band is fixed" and "we need an answer by Friday", in Megan's voice. Drafts only; she sends or says it.

## Offer comparison

Ask for these inputs before building:

- base;
- target bonus and realistic attainment;
- equity with valuation assumption, vesting and cliff;
- signing bonus;
- benefits differences;
- relocation;
- travel and office days;
- expected billability;
- reporting line and title;
- anything verified in writing about promotion.

Show base apart from everything else, with a year-one and a four-year view. Lay out the gates per offer, the matrix with its three columns, the weighted score, the strongest case for each offer and the open questions on each. Do not pick. Two or more offers or scenarios go in a Codex Sheets artifact; a single offer goes in a Codex doc. Save once under `03_Tracker/` with a pointer from each role folder. Tracker status (`offer`, `closed`) changes only on Megan's word.

## Reporting

Everything Megan reads or sends goes through `megan-writing-style` and `writing-integrity`, and `/usr/bin/python3 ~/.agents/humanize/tellscan.py scan <file> --profile megan` where installed; otherwise check by reading and say no scan ran. Update the role work record and tracker. End with changed, verified, unchanged and the exact next action.

Method adapted from the open-source ResumeSkills set (offer-comparison-analyzer, salary-negotiation-prep, job-description-analyzer red flags, interview-prep-generator questions), rebuilt around the October 7, 2026 career direction.

skills.title: Case Study Builder
skills.description: Turn a piece of Megan's work into a sanitized, evidence-checked portfolio case study (working + publish copy) using her template and publish gate.
skills.markdown:
---
name: "case-study-builder"
description: "Turn a piece of Megan's work into a sanitized, evidence-checked portfolio case study (working + publish copy) using her template and publish gate."
---

# Case Study Builder

Turn any project, product, or engagement of Megan's into a portfolio case study that is consistent, sanitized, and safe to publish. Produce two copies every time: a **working copy** (evidence labels and proof notes visible, for Megan) and a **publish copy** (clean first-person prose, for the site).

The split is the point. Evidence control lives in the working copy. The publish copy states what happened with confidence and contains no labels, caveat sentences, or status notes.

## Before you start
- Megan works independently through Live Laugh Code LLC. Use the current claims and rights ledger for reuse and publication decisions about Meridian, the Knowledge Hub, the skills architecture, and the playbooks. Client names, logos, client data, rate-card numbers, margins, and quote identifiers stay out.
- Use the current career numbers from `/Volumes/BeastMode/AIMemory/JobHunt/` (the program records and evidence ledger). Don't invent or round past them.
- Never invent a fact, number, client, or quote to make a study read better. Missing detail: bracket it in the working copy and flag it to Megan in chat; do not fill the gap.

## Skeleton (fill for each study)
- **Title** — what she built or did, plain, no client name.
- **Client (sanitized)** — industry + size band only; never name, logo, or identifying detail. If it's her own product, say so.
- **Problem** — the business problem, one short paragraph.
- **What I did** — the approach and the system or artifacts she actually built.
- **How it works** — the mechanism (the differentiator; show the build, not just the result).
- **Outcome** — what happened, stated plainly.
- **My role** — what she personally did versus the team.
- **What it becomes** — the reusable method, offer, or skill it maps to.

Write each study in first person, as Megan. Do NOT add a closing "The point" / summary paragraph — it restates the piece, which she cuts every time.

## Evidence labels (working copy only)
- **[verified]** — source is showable (a record, a computed figure).
- **[reported]** — a real engagement figure not independently re-verified.
- **[estimated]** — a modeled/opportunity number.
- **[in progress]** — built, not yet in production use.
An untagged number does not ship.

## Resolving labels into the publish copy
Labels come off. Caveat sentences do not replace them.
- [verified] → state it.
- [estimated] → keep the single word inside the claim: "an estimated $660K–$1.07M." Nothing more.
- [reported] → use it only if Megan would say it plainly ("a colleague's scoped playbook went from two weeks to half a day"). Otherwise cut it. Never append "directional" or "not a controlled study."
- [in progress] → describe what she built and what it does. Do not add "not in production," "not verified," or "not claimed." Don't imply it runs live; just don't say either way.
- Lost or open deals → one word in the outcome ("lost," "open") when the outcome matters to the story. No status sentence.

Banned in the publish copy: "not verified," "unverified," "not claimed," "I don't claim," "does not prove," "directional," "not a controlled study," "Where it stood," "remained outside," "no sold deal was recorded," any sentence explaining what a number is not, and any state or publication note. These make Megan sound unsure and devalue her work. If a claim needs one of them to be safe, cut the claim.

## Voice — run the publish copy through megan-writing-style
The publish copy is Megan's own first-person voice, so gate it against the `megan-writing-style` skill before it ships. Her hard rules, applied here:
- Trust the reader — never restate a point or explain the previous sentence.
- No empty "builder" constructions ("I build systems that turn X into Y"). Name the actual thing: a deal-intelligence system, a discovery-to-requirements engine, the playbook catalog.
- No X-not-Y antithesis ("systems, not slideware"; "deprecate deliberately, not delete"). State the positive directly.
- No defensive disclaimers (rule 6).
- No origin-story throat-clearing; no banned phrases ("at the intersection of," "proven ability to," "whether it's X or Y," "at the end of the day," and the rest in her profile).
- Concrete nouns, real numbers, named systems in every sentence. Short sentences mixed with long. End flat and confident on the last true thing.

## Publish gate (all six before it goes public)
1. **Sanitized** — no client name, logo, stakeholder, internal identifier, or their dollar figures unless Megan cleared them.
2. **Owned** — methods and products she may show; no rate card or margin.
3. **Sourced** — every number in the working copy carries a label; nothing in the publish copy overstates its label.
4. **Separation** — no internal resourcing, rate card, margin, or staffing detail.
5. **In her voice and clean** — passes megan-writing-style; a scan for the banned disclaimer phrases returns nothing.
6. **Two versions** — working copy (labels, proof notes) + publish copy (clean prose).

## Metadata block (top of the working copy only)
```
Study:            <name>
Maps to offer:    <offer / skill>
Evidence status:  <verified | mostly reported | mostly estimated>
Sanitization:     <done | pending>
Ownership check:  <clear | needs generic rebuild>
Publish-ready:    <yes | no — blocked on: ...>
```
The metadata block never appears in the publish copy.

## Output
Deliver the study as a markdown file: metadata block, then working copy, then publish copy. Save durable versions to the project. Report bracketed gaps and figures that need Megan's confirmation in chat, not in the publish copy.

The publish copy is Megan's own first-person voice, so gate it against the megan-writing-style skill before it ships. Her hard rules, applied here:

  • Trust the reader — never restate a point or explain the previous sentence.
  • No empty "builder" constructions ("I build systems that turn X into Y"). Name the actual thing: a deal-intelligence system, a discovery-to-requirements engine, the playbook catalog.
  • No X-not-Y antithesis ("systems, not slideware"; "deprecate deliberately, not delete"). State the positive directly.
  • No defensive disclaimers (rule 6).
  • No origin-story throat-clearing; no banned phrases ("at the intersection of," "proven ability to," "whether it's X or Y," "at the end of the day," and the rest in her profile).
  • Concrete nouns, real numbers, named systems in every sentence. Short sentences mixed with long. End flat and confident on the last true thing.

  1. Sanitized — no client name, logo, stakeholder, internal identifier, or their dollar figures unless Megan cleared them.
  2. Owned — methods and products she may show; no rate card or margin.
  3. Sourced — every number in the working copy carries a label; nothing in the publish copy overstates its label.
  4. Separation — no internal resourcing, rate card, margin, or staffing detail.
  5. In her voice and clean — passes megan-writing-style; a scan for the banned disclaimer phrases returns nothing.
  6. Two versions — working copy (labels, proof notes) + publish copy (clean prose).

Study:            <name>
Maps to offer:    <offer / skill>
Evidence status:  <verified | mostly reported | mostly estimated>
Sanitization:     <done | pending>

Publish-ready:    <yes | no — blocked on: ...>

The metadata block never appears in the publish copy.

Deliver the study as a markdown file: metadata block, then working copy, then publish copy. Save durable versions to the project. Report bracketed gaps and figures that need Megan's confirmation in chat, not in the publish copy.

skills.title: Code Simplify
skills.description: Review and refine the current code change for reuse, clarity, maintainability, and efficiency without changing behavior. Use when a delivery workflow requires a simplify pass, when the user asks to simplify or clean up a diff, or before committing a non-trivial implementation. Scope work to the current branch diff or an explicit target, preserve public behavior and project conventions, apply only high-confidence edits, and verify the result with focused tests. This is the Codex-native equivalent of Claude Code review with fixes, not a prose-style pass.
skills.markdown:
---
name: code-simplify
description: 'Review and refine the current code change for reuse, clarity, maintainability, and efficiency without changing behavior. Use when a delivery workflow requires a simplify pass, when the user asks to simplify or clean up a diff, or before committing a non-trivial implementation. Scope work to the current branch diff or an explicit target, preserve public behavior and project conventions, apply only high-confidence edits, and verify the result with focused tests. This is the Codex-native equivalent of Claude Code review with fixes, not a prose-style pass.'
---

# Code Simplify

Make the current change easier to understand and maintain without changing what it does. This is
a judgment pass over code, not a formatter, prose rewrite, or license to redesign the feature.

## Scope

Use the explicit target when the caller supplies one. Otherwise inspect:

1. commits ahead of the branch's upstream or merge base;
2. staged and unstaged changes;
3. untracked source files that belong to the change.

Read the repository's `AGENTS.md`, nearby tests, and the surrounding implementation before editing.
Generated output, vendored code, lockfiles, snapshots, and unrelated pre-existing changes stay out
of scope unless the caller explicitly includes them.

## Review lenses

- **Reuse:** replace new duplication with an established local helper or pattern when the fit is
  exact and the result is clearer.
- **Clarity:** reduce needless nesting, indirection, branching, and naming ambiguity.
- **Maintainability:** keep responsibilities narrow, make invariants visible, and remove dead code
  introduced by the current change.
- **Efficiency:** remove repeated or unnecessary work when the improvement is evident and does not
  trade away readability or correctness.

Do not chase cleverness, minimum line count, or speculative abstraction. A slightly longer direct
implementation is better than a compressed one that hides behavior.

## Behavior boundary

Preserve public APIs, data shapes, permissions, ordering, error behavior, logging semantics,
user-facing strings, prompts, test expectations, and integration contracts. Do not weaken checks
or delete apparently redundant safeguards without proving why they are redundant. If a proposed
cleanup would change any of these, report it as a separate recommendation instead of applying it.

## Workflow

1. Establish the diff base and list the files in scope. Stop if the base is ambiguous or the
   repository has overlapping changes that cannot be separated safely.
2. Inspect the diff with enough surrounding code and tests to understand its behavior.
3. Record candidate improvements under the four review lenses. Reject speculative, cosmetic-only,
   or behavior-changing candidates.
4. Apply the smallest coherent set of high-confidence edits.
5. Run the narrowest relevant formatter, static checks, and focused tests. Run broader repository
   gates when its contract requires them.
6. Re-read the final diff against the original intent. Confirm that no unrelated file or protected
   behavior changed.
7. Report applied refinements, verification evidence, and worthwhile candidates deliberately left
   unapplied.

For a review-only request, stop after step 3 and return findings without editing.

## Host routing

OpenAI Codex agents run this skill directly. Current Claude Code can use
`/code-review medium --fix` for the corresponding review-and-apply step, then inspect its resulting
diff and run the repository's required tests. The delivery contract names both routes so it does
not depend on one vendor's built-in command vocabulary.

skills.title: Cutover closeout
skills.description: Prepare a cutover runbook, go-live acceptance record, hypercare plan, and delivery closeout from the approved release and executed scope.
skills.markdown:
---
name: cutover-closeout
description: "Prepare a cutover runbook, go-live acceptance record, hypercare plan, and delivery closeout from the approved release and executed scope."
---

# Cutover closeout

Read [shared workflow](references/estate/workflow.md). For a rendered or branded artifact, read [brand policy](references/estate/brand.md) before choosing visual values. These references are generated from the canonical policies when the estate builds.

Read the release plan, test results, actual go/no-go decision, executed scope, acceptance rules, and support ownership. Preparing a runbook is allowed before approval; executing cutover depends on the authorization and target environment.

For each cutover step, specify owner, prerequisites, action, expected result, validation, timing, and rollback or stop condition. Order dependencies explicitly. Identify the last reversible point and who can make the go/no-go decision. Never invent a successful rehearsal or rollback test.

Track go-live acceptance against the agreement's actual criteria. Record open defects and agreed dispositions. Deemed acceptance applies only if the governing agreement contains it and its conditions are evidenced; elapsed time alone is insufficient.

During hypercare, track impact, severity, owner, workaround, resolution, and confirmation. Closeout covers deliverables, acceptance, access and support transition, remaining obligations, operational documentation, and lessons. Distinguish technical deployment, business acceptance, support handover, and project closure in the final record.

skills.markdown:
---
name: execution-truth
description: Establish and verify the actual completion state of work that changes repositories, files, cloud documents, deployments, client data, publications, installations, or automations. Use before material implementation and at handoff. Do not use for ordinary questions, explanations, or read-only analysis with no produced artifact or state change.
---

# Execution truth

Prevent a local draft, commit, successful command, or API response from being
reported as a later state.

At the start, identify the requested outcome, authoritative source, finish line,
affected systems, and prohibited actions. Keep one independently reviewable
objective in scope. Record adjacent findings as follow-ups unless they block the
finish line.

Read only the adapter for the current work:

- Repository or code change: [`references/git.md`](references/git.md)
- Local artifact or filesystem change: [`references/local-files.md`](references/local-files.md)
- Google Drive or another cloud document: [`references/cloud-documents.md`](references/cloud-documents.md)
- Environment or application deployment: [`references/deployments.md`](references/deployments.md)
- Client records or migration: [`references/client-data.md`](references/client-data.md)
- Website, bundle, or marketplace publication: [`references/publishing.md`](references/publishing.md)
- Scheduled or recurring work: [`references/automations.md`](references/automations.md)

Use `scripts/work_truth.py` for a bounded Git, file, or generic receipt when the
runtime can execute it. A runtime without the script performs the adapter's
read-only checks and labels unavailable proof instead of assuming success.

Use these states precisely: `proposed`, `built-locally`, `committed-locally`,
`pr-open`, `merged`, `published`, `installed`, and `verified-live`. A task may
need a more specific adapter state, but it may never promote itself without
evidence from the destination system.

Finish with four facts: **changed now**, **verified**, **still unchanged**, and
the **exact next action**. Name any approval required for that next action.

description: Work with repositories owned by mshellman-llc using the shared authenticated GitHub CLI and Git. Use for repository access, commits, pushes, pull requests, releases, and repository deployment workflows.
